generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the usual referencing style is APA, an author-date style with its own rules. Your department will confirm it, and once it is set the task is to apply it to every citation and reference without slips. A marker reads your reference list to judge how widely you have read, and often turns to it first. In psychology, where claims rest on bodies of evidence, a full and consistent list shows the scope of your research.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students hand in essays, each with a reference list.

Tom has read widely, but his reference list mixes styles. Some entries give the year in brackets and others do not; some article titles are in italics and others in quotation marks; one citation uses a number. The marker cannot tell at a glance how carefully the sources were handled, and the inconsistency undercuts otherwise good research.

Amara has read the same sources and used APA throughout. Every citation matches a full reference, every reference follows the same pattern, and the list is alphabetical. The marker sees the scope of her reading at once, and the consistency reads as care and competence.

Both students did the reading. Only Amara's citation let the marker see it.
generatedProse.summary: A referencing style is a set of rules for laying out citations and references, and in psychology that style is usually APA. What matters most is consistency: one style, applied to every citation and reference. Done well, your reference list shows a marker the scope and care of your research, and earns marks against the criteria. You can now cite, reference and apply APA with purpose in your psychology writing.

check.body: In the worked example, why did Amara's reference list work in her favour with the marker?

items.text: One consistent style let the marker see the scope of her reading at a glance.
It listed more sources than Tom's did.
It used an unusual style that stood out.
It placed the references at the start of the essay.

feedback.correct: That's right. A single consistent style let the marker take in the scope of her reading at once.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Both students read the same sources, so what made the difference?
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's list worked because one consistent style let the marker see the scope of her reading at a glance.
